Personal project · 2026

EIDOLON
TAROT

Not to predict the future, but to see ourselves.

A tarot concept about self-discovery, expressed through book-shaped packaging, original cards and an interactive guidebook.

Nearly every visual asset was drawn by hand in Figma.

Explore the prototype ↗
RoleSolo designer
ToolFigma
TypeCourse project
FocusVisual design · Variants · Prototyping
01 / Concept

From a book to a mirror.

I wanted tarot to become a way of looking inward, rather than simply a tool for divination.

01 — IDEA

Tarot book

I began with an interactive tarot book featuring five cutout windows inspired by a card spread.

02 — PIVOT

Book-shaped box

I reconsidered the standalone book and carried its form into packaging for an original tarot deck.

03 — SYMBOL

Eye in a mirror

I combined an eye and a mirror into a central motif representing introspection and identity.

02 / Visual identity

Mystical, yet soft.

Lavender and pale gold create a dreamlike atmosphere, paired with classical serif typography and simplified symbols.

A Journey Into the Self
A Journey Into the Self

Drawn by hand in Figma

From stars, moons and suns to eyes, mirrors and butterflies, I drew the card illustrations and nearly all visual assets myself in Figma. The ornate border on the book-shaped packaging is the only AI-generated visual asset retained in the final design.

03 / The three cards

Three ways to see yourself.

Inspired by Rider–Waite–Smith, I hand-drew and simplified traditional imagery in Figma into a journey from reflection to illusion to awakening.

↻ Click to flip

Reflection

A golden star above reflective waves, inspired by water and the myth of Narcissus.

↻ Click to flip

Illusion

A crescent moon and a single eye explore perception, dreams and uncertainty.

↻ Click to flip

Awakening

A butterfly emerges against a glowing sun, symbolizing transformation and self-acceptance.

04 / Guidebook

Making discovery feel natural.

From a fold-out guide to a six-page booklet, the design evolved toward a more natural reading and unboxing experience.

FORMAT

Three double-sided sheets

The folding interaction felt unnatural, so I switched to a six-page booklet.

COLOR

A brighter purple

A brighter purple distinguishes the guidebook from the rest of the set.

GRADIENT

Diamond gradient

Replacing the linear gradient creates a softer, luminous appearance.

05 / Interaction

Open. Discover. Explore.

Component variants organize the packaging states, while clicks and automatic page transitions create a continuous exploration sequence.

06 / Reflection

Beyond the visuals.

This project shifted my focus from illustration alone toward variants and prototyping, and how a design is actually experienced.

Interaction iteration

Self-testing revealed that drag interactions were less intuitive. I replaced them with clicks and used After Delay for a quick guidebook preview.

Asset transparency

AI-generated references were explored during ideation. The ornate packaging border was the only AI-generated visual asset retained in the final design; the card illustrations and symbolic elements were manually created in Figma.
